semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Image editing involves operations that change or enhance images, which is semantically equivalent to image processing. Both domains involve manipulating images to achieve a desired result.

parent_domains.justification: Imaging is a broad field encompassing all activities related to the creation, processing, and manipulation of images, of which image editing is a specific sub-domain.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Among the identified parent domains, imaging is the closest parent domain as it broadly covers aspects of both creation and processing, providing a framework under which image editing is a subset.

child_domains.justification: Image completion is a task often included in image editing, where missing or occluded parts of an image are filled, making it a more specific domain within image editing.
Image segmentation can be a part of image editing, where the image is divided into segments to isolate parts of the image. This is often a step in more advanced editing tasks.

closest_child_domain.justification: Image completion is directly linked to image editing as it involves editing an image to complete or restore it, closely aligning with typical image editing tasks.

sibling_domains.justification: Image synthesis involves creating new images, which can relate to image editing when it entails modifying synthesized images.
Image generation closely involves creating entire images afresh, which can be related to image editing when generated images are subsequently edited.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Image synthesis is the closest sibling domain because it frequently involves generating realistic images that may require subsequent editing, hence closely tangent to image editing.

unrelated_domains.justification: Medical image analysis is highly domain-specific, focusing on medical diagnostics rather than general image editing applications.
Video synthesis pertains to creating new videos, which is only indirectly related to image editing through potential frame editing.
Video generation involves creating videos, distinct from static image editing tasks.
While there's overlap, computer graphics generally focuses on generating graphical content, possibly involving more complex rendering than typical image editing tasks.
Text-to-image synthesis focuses on creating images from textual descriptions, a distinct process from image editing.
This is analogous to text-to-image synthesis, creating image content from text rather than editing existing content.
This domain is related to converting text directly into image representations, a different task from editing images.
This evaluates the consistency between textual descriptions and generated images, which is analytically different from editing tasks.
Focuses on training models on both images and text, which is less directly related to editing existing images.
This domain focuses on identifying objects or patterns within images rather than editing them.
Image retrieval involves finding and fetching images based on specific criteria rather than editing them.
While it involves processing images, it focuses on extracting data and understanding from images, distinct from editing.
Involves comparing images for similarities or correspondences rather than editing the images themselves.
Focuses on reducing image size without losing quality significantly, which can be a part of editing but is not central to it.
